name: Caribbean Netherlands (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba)
summary_text: Caribbean Netherlands (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba): public bodies of the Netherlands — Dutch equality law applies directly but small, more religious island societies. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: Netherlands (0.79) plus a local delta of -0.10. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Safety and travel information - Pride Amsterdam 2027
sources.claim_summary: WorldPride Amsterdam 2026 safety and travel page (about the Netherlands, included here because Caribbean Netherlands is part of the Kingdom): covers border/airport procedures, the Schengen rule that foreign nationals must carry passports, Schiphol logistics, and a dedicated section for transgender and non-binary visitors. Notes the Netherlands ranks #13 on the ILGA Rainbow Map 2026.

sources.title: Netherlands | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for the Netherlands (updated March 2026): progressive laws with gaps - legal gender change still requires a medical expert letter; nonbinary 'X' marker only via a 3-9 month court procedure; the Transgender Act (self-ID) was withdrawn in July 2025. Caribbean Netherlands (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba) follows Dutch law as special municipalities.

ILGA World Trans Legal Mapping Report 2019 (3rd edition): global mapping of legal gender recognition laws and policies by country/territory - includes the Dutch Caribbean (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba follow Dutch LGR framework as special municipalities).

sources.title: Top 10 destinations that celebrate marriage equality in the Caribbean and Latin America
sources.claim_summary: GayCities (Dec 2022): top 10 Caribbean/Latin American destinations celebrating marriage equality - travel-oriented overview for same-sex couples planning destination weddings.

Dutch Caribbean Legal Portal (Dec 2012): the first same-sex wedding in Caribbean Netherlands, performed on Saba for two visiting residents - Saba was the first island of the former Netherlands Antilles to facilitate same-sex weddings after the 2010 constitutional status change.

sources.title: Weddings | Saba Tourism
sources.claim_summary: Saba Tourism official weddings page: markets the island for destination weddings (civil ceremonies at the Court Room, flexible registrar) - relevant as Saba performs same-sex marriages under Dutch law.
